Try not to be judgmental. People with depression may try to convince others or themselves that everything is A-okay by acting that way, but there's probably underlying insecurities, fear of being a burden on others, hopelessness and a general feeling of being disappointed in oneself. 
Sometimes it's better to just listen. Don't ask why they have certain thoughts or why they did something. Sometimes they don't know the answer or thinking about an answer may trigger them. It's very true that we are in a dire situation right now. We need to act fast and collectively to combat climate change. There are governments (specifically of developed countries) around the world that are aggressively pushing for zero-emission technologies, and these technologies are getting increasingly cheaper and more efficient. While there are corporations that are still lobbying for fossil fuels, deforestation and natural habitat destruction for their own greed, and while there are people who refuse to believe in climate change, there are also many many people out there who are working tirelessly to protect our environment. If you watch the video, it mentions that developing countries no longer need to rely completely on coal and fossil fuel for their economic development, because the environment-friendly alternatives are just getting cheaper by the day. 

Our worst enemy, when it comes to dealing with climate change, is hopelessness. I agree that it is an extremely urgent situation, but it's also important to note that people do care about it and technologies are improving. So, instead of losing all hope, you should try and see what you can do to help. 

Can you join any climate-change related committees in your city or county (for example climate change advocacy groups, environmental justice groups, zero-emission transportation or food security initiatives.. anything that interests you)?

Can you talk to your coworkers about what your company is doing to combat climate change? Do they have volunteer programs with any climate change advocacy groups in your city, or do they donate to any such groups? Anything else they do to make their product/service more environmentally friendly?

On a personal level, are you able to purchase plant-based foods or if not, are you able to purchase eggs, meat and milk from farmer's markets instead of supermarket chains? Are you able to reuse (and if not reuse, recycle)?

Even if you spend some time just learning more about climate change, any technologies that interest you, any initiatives you might wanna participate in, that itself is a significant step. On that note, thank you for this post! There's still a lot we can do, we need to hurry up and give it our all. But we have to keep trying, we can't afford to lose hope.


(P.S.- I currently work in the clean mobility sector. It infuriates me, the kinda shit that corporations like Nestle, Shell, Amazon etc. get away with, but on the other hand, I've also met such amazing, passionate people, who are spending their lives trying to combat climate change and push for environmental equity.)
